item.title: Snap‑O 14.0.0
item.description:
14.0.0

  • Connect to remote ADB servers over SSH, with saved connections you can enable or disable.
  • Improve Live Preview and touch input support for Android environments where AVC encoding and uinput are not available.
  • Speed up Live Preview startup.

13.1.0

  • Trim screen recordings before saving or sharing them.
  • Open devices and emulators directly with snapo:// links.
  • Show the same device in multiple Live Preview windows.
  • Recover automatically when the local ADB server is missing.
  • Keep floating device controls anchored outside the window.
  • Confirm before discarding a capture with Escape, and fix saving captures to selected folders.
  • Follow new network requests in either sort order while preserving your position when browsing older requests.
  • Show development server overrides in inspector menus.
  • Strengthen authentication for the Android helper service.

13.0.2

  • No more prompt when discarding unsaved captures.

13.0.1

  • Fixed dragging full and cropped recordings from capture review into apps such as Slack, with accurate video previews and export progress.

13.0.0

  • Review and crop screenshots or recordings before saving them to Capture History or dragging a copy into another app.
  • Use ⇧⌘V to both start and stop recording.
  • Android tool builds recover automatically from damaged managed Node installations.

12.0.0

  • Type, copy, and paste directly in Live Preview.
  • Screen recording now has a live preview so you can continue interacting with the device in Snap-O while you record.
  • Rotate physical devices and emulators with the same controls and keyboard shortcuts.
  • Use new capture shortcuts: ⇧⌘S for screenshots, ⇧⌘V for recording, and ⌘Y for Capture History.
  • Delete selected captures with Delete or ⌘Delete.

11.2.0

  • Select multiple captures in Capture History and delete them together.
  • Start Live Preview faster.
  • Recognize running emulators sooner and keep device names consistent across windows.
  • Fix a crash when an emulator connection fails or is cancelled.
  • Place Volume Up above Volume Down in the left control bar.

11.1.0

  • Floating device control bar with Back, Home, app switcher, volume, power, and supported emulator controls.
  • Two-finger gestures: hold Option before clicking and dragging. Hold Shift as well to move both touch points together.
  • Drag files into Live Preview to copy them to your device or emulator. Drop APKs to install them.
  • Emulator Live Preview now uses gRPC screen streaming, so you can see the screen earlier during boot.
  • Clipboard sync between your Mac and the device in the focused Live Preview window.
  • Fixed an issue where one device disconnecting or failing could stop recordings on other devices.

11.0.0

  • New: Device Manager -- Manage existing Android emulators and connected devices. Start, stop, or cold boot emulators, then open them directly in Live Preview.
  • Command-drag instead of Option-drag from Live Preview to export a screenshot while ordinary dragging controls the device.

Device Manager uses your existing Android SDK and AVDs. SDK installation, AVD creation and editing, and a custom SDK location picker are not included in this version.

10.1.0

  • Device previews in Live Preview make it easier to see which screen you’re switching to.
  • Capture names carry through when saving or sharing screenshots and recordings.
  • Live Preview connects automatically when Android finishes booting.

10.0.0

  • Capture History keeps screenshots and recordings after windows close or Snap-O restarts. Name captures and manage storage and retention.
  • Copy screenshots with visible confirmation, and copy Network request text, cURL commands, and images without extra confirmation prompts.
  • Tool choices refresh correctly when an inspected app restarts or you switch processes.
  • Show or hide the Capture and Tool panes from the View menu, and open Capture History from the toolbar.
  • Updated the app icon with a green aperture and starfield.

For tool authors, normal Gradle builds now use the frontend lockfile. Run installSnapoToolDependencies when you need to update dependencies.

9.0.0

Upgrade requirements

  • Requires macOS 26 or later.
  • Upgrade your Android Network and Tweaks dependencies to 9.0.0 and rebuild your app alongside this Mac update. The new tool protocols are incompatible with 8.0.0 clients and libraries. Keep using Snap-O 8.0.0 if you cannot update macOS or rebuild your Android app yet.

What's new

  • Tools now ship their frontends inside Android libraries. Network and Tweaks load the frontend that matches the installed app, allowing tools to evolve independently of the Mac app.
  • Build custom tools with the Tool Packager Gradle plugin and Android core library. The Gradle plugin bundles the host JavaScript SDK and prepares the frontend automatically.
  • Set your app's tool order with snapo.tool_order manifest metadata.
  • Network and Tweaks have independent Python CLIs, available directly or through snapo network and snapo tweaks.
  • The native tool picker manages app selection and reconnection, and explains when an installed tool needs updating.
  • The Mac app now runs in App Sandbox.

Full changelog

8.0.0

  • New Tweak type: Bézier curves.
  • Collapse Tweaks sections and adjust values with more compact sliders.

6.0.0

  • Prototype Android API changes with Python route handlers. Mock or modify responses, add delays, and reload edits while the app runs.
  • Try API overrides with the shared Tasks demos for OkHttp and Ktor.

API overrides require the Snap-O 6.0.0 Android OkHttp integration. HttpURLConnection and WebSocket traffic remain inspection-only.

5.1.0

  • Open Android apps from Network and Tweaks inspector waiting screens.
  • Select an available app at startup when the previous app or inspector is unavailable.
  • Retry failed Live Preview connections with Connect instead of repeated automatic attempts.
  • Fix an issue where the Android keyboard could repeatedly show and hide while Live Preview was connecting.
  • Fix wobbling loading indicators.

5.0.0

Live Preview

  • Snap-O now opens in Live Preview by default.
  • Hold Option and drag from the preview to share a screenshot.
  • Smoother dragging when controlling your device, with lower CPU use.

App Inspector

  • Network and Tweaks share one picker row per running app process.
  • Inspector selection and captured content are preserved across reconnects.

Network Inspector

  • Save exclusion filters to hide recurring traffic, or exclude a host by right-clicking a request.
  • Clearer request details and SSE status, with explanations for unavailable response bodies and a Retry button for failed loads.
  • Fixed arrow-key navigation and copying request details, payloads, and stream events.

4.1.0

  • Inspect and adjust app-owned settings live, including values shared across Compose components.
  • Select Kotlin enum values and run app-defined actions from the Mac inspector, Android overlay, or Snap-O CLI.
  • Track changed settings accurately and reset them using each app's own reset behavior.
  • Apply valid tweak edits even when another edit in the same batch is rejected.
  • Keep app discovery responsive when another connected Android app freezes.
  • Accept tweak text values beginning with a dash in the CLI.
  • Android integration: place SnapOTweakOverlay() after app content in a fullscreen Box; the previous content-wrapping overload was removed.

4.0.0

  • Introducing Snap-O Tweaks: adjust Android colors, typography, animations, text, and other UI values live.
  • Edit tweaks from the Mac App Inspector or a floating Android overlay.
  • Find previously adjusted tweaks even after leaving their screen.
  • Switch between Network and Tweaks inspection for each connected app.
  • Inspect network requests and view, change, reset, or watch tweaks using the Snap-O CLI and Codex skills.
  • Live Preview displays static screens and final frames more reliably.
  • Network capture correctly handles request bodies that close their output stream.
  • The Logcat viewer has been removed.

3.2.0

  • Live Preview starts faster and supports Android’s “Show taps.”
  • Network Inspector is faster, reconnects more reliably, shows when responses are still loading, and previews images.
  • Cleaner capture screen and minor workspace improvements.

3.1.0

  • Window/layout improvements and bug fixes
  • Recorded video stops playback when window is completely obscured

3.0.0

  • Network Inspector is no longer a separate, inner helper app.
  • You can toggle the Capture and Network Inspector views separately per window.
  • In other words, if you only use Network Inspector, you could hide the Capture View, and every new window will just show you the Network Inspector.
  • A new native toolbar for Network Inspector.
  • Since it now uses a WKWebView instead of Electron, download size is back down to the tiniest it's ever been: ~2.36MB.

2.1.1

  • Snap-O's window toolbar is now two lines, making it possible to see all the buttons.
  • Richer network inspector guide.

2.0.1

Network Inspector

  • Breaking change: Protocol has changed. Snap-O servers are now feature-based. You will need to have Snap-O Network Inspector 2.0.1 to inspect network requests for apps that include snapo-link-android 2.0.1
  • Network Inspector is now an Electron-based app
  • Now distributed via DMG

1.0.0

This rollup includes the changes that landed in 0.21.2 and 0.21.3 (those weren’t pushed as standalone official releases).

Why 1.0.0 now

  • jpackage DMG packaging doesn’t allow a 0 major version! so we needed to move off 0.x.
  • Snap-O has also come a long way in reliability and UX, so it might be a good point for a major milestone anyways.

Updates

  • New CLI tool: added snapo network ... commands for request/event inspection directly from terminal.
  • Export HAR (sanitized): added export support (sanitized by default), plus remembered export folder.
  • Multi-window + multi-client support: better behavior when multiple app windows/connections are active.
  • CDP-based network inspection: moved to a Chrome DevTools Protocol-style network model, with better event semantics.
  • General polish: dependency/build updates and small UI cleanups across the desktop inspector.

0.19.0

  • Fix Network Inspector app icon sizing
  • Exclusion URL filter
  • Better handling of large (e.g. 3+MB JSON payloads)

Exclusion filters in the search field:

  • data will match "data"
  • -data will match anything that doesn't contain "data"
  • "-data" will match "-data"
  • -"-data" will match anything that doesn't contain "-data"

0.18.0

Network Inspector is now a helper app written with Kotlin Multiplatform. It's still packaged inside Snap-O.app, but as an inner helper app.

Now that KMP has been introduced, it'd be nice if everything ended up with KMP. With a nice AVPlayerView in a Swing panel, maybe it's possible..

0.17.0

Some payload format updates.

Network events are now wrapped in a "FeatureEvent" payload wrapper, to support other features sending messages via the "Snap-O Link Server" in the future.

0.16.0

Liquid glass support

0.15.0

  • Max response payload size: 5MB
  • Image preview support
  • Change sort order of network requests
  • "Waiting for ADB server..." alert will not trigger while Snap-O is in the background.

0.14.1

Maintains window order when re-opening Snap-O.

0.14.0

Logcat Viewer by @angus-oai

Tools now available from the capture window toolbar.

0.13.0

Network Inspector will re-open on launch.

0.12.0

Collapsible JSON pretty printing view
More performant handling of large response bodies

0.11.0

Early work on network inspector (alpha)

0.10.0

  1. "Bug Report" option for screen recording (--bugreport)
  2. "Show Touches on Capture" works again
  3. Preview strip improvements: Drag 'n drop from the thumbnails, and device name hints
  4. Ensure each simultaneous capture gets a unique filename

0.9.0

Removed most of the animated transitions throughout the app, to make it feel even snappier.

0.8.0

Simultaneous device captures

Don't capture the wrong device by accident, anymore. Capture all of them!

  1. When you take a screenshot or screen recording, Snap-O does it across all your connected devices simultaneously.
  2. Next/Previous Device now moves between the captures you had just taken.
  3. Screen recordings only show up if they have a non-zero duration.

0.7.0

Snap-O floats over other windows during a screen recording, to make it easier to use alongside an emulator in Android Studio.

0.6.0

  1. Faster time to first screenshot
  2. ADB path no longer needs to be set
  3. Live Preview has some basic touch support
  4. Other UX/perf improvements

0.5.0

Initial Snap-O release!

  • Clearer request details and SSE status, with explanations for unavailable response bodies and a Retry button for failed loads.
  • Fixed arrow-key navigation and copying request details, payloads, and stream events.

4.1.0

  • Inspect and adjust app-owned settings live, including values shared across Compose components.
  • Select Kotlin enum values and run app-defined actions from the Mac inspector, Android overlay, or Snap-O CLI.
  • Track changed settings accurately and reset them using each app's own reset behavior.
  • Apply valid tweak edits even when another edit in the same batch is rejected.
  • Keep app discovery responsive when another connected Android app freezes.
  • Accept tweak text values beginning with a dash in the CLI.
  • Android integration: place SnapOTweakOverlay() after app content in a fullscreen Box; the previous content-wrapping overload was removed.

4.0.0

  • Introducing Snap-O Tweaks: adjust Android colors, typography, animations, text, and other UI values live.
  • Edit tweaks from the Mac App Inspector or a floating Android overlay.
  • Find previously adjusted tweaks even after leaving their screen.
  • Switch between Network and Tweaks inspection for each connected app.
  • Inspect network requests and view, change, reset, or watch tweaks using the Snap-O CLI and Codex skills.
  • Live Preview displays static screens and final frames more reliably.
  • Network capture correctly handles request bodies that close their output stream.
  • The Logcat viewer has been removed.

3.2.0

  • Live Preview starts faster and supports Android’s “Show taps.”
  • Network Inspector is faster, reconnects more reliably, shows when responses are still loading, and previews images.
  • Cleaner capture screen and minor workspace improvements.

3.1.0

  • Window/layout improvements and bug fixes
  • Recorded video stops playback when window is completely obscured

3.0.0

  • Network Inspector is no longer a separate, inner helper app.
  • You can toggle the Capture and Network Inspector views separately per window.
  • In other words, if you only use Network Inspector, you could hide the Capture View, and every new window will just show you the Network Inspector.
  • A new native toolbar for Network Inspector.
  • Since it now uses a WKWebView instead of Electron, download size is back down to the tiniest it's ever been: ~2.36MB.

2.1.1

  • Snap-O's window toolbar is now two lines, making it possible to see all the buttons.
  • Richer network inspector guide.

2.0.1

Network Inspector

  • Breaking change: Protocol has changed. Snap-O servers are now feature-based. You will need to have Snap-O Network Inspector 2.0.1 to inspect network requests for apps that include snapo-link-android 2.0.1
  • Network Inspector is now an Electron-based app
  • Now distributed via DMG

1.0.0

This rollup includes the changes that landed in 0.21.2 and 0.21.3 (those weren’t pushed as standalone official releases).

Why 1.0.0 now

  • jpackage DMG packaging doesn’t allow a 0 major version! so we needed to move off 0.x.
  • Snap-O has also come a long way in reliability and UX, so it might be a good point for a major milestone anyways.

Updates

  • New CLI tool: added snapo network ... commands for request/event inspection directly from terminal.
  • Export HAR (sanitized): added export support (sanitized by default), plus remembered export folder.
  • Multi-window + multi-client support: better behavior when multiple app windows/connections are active.
  • CDP-based network inspection: moved to a Chrome DevTools Protocol-style network model, with better event semantics.
  • General polish: dependency/build updates and small UI cleanups across the desktop inspector.

0.19.0

  • Fix Network Inspector app icon sizing
  • Exclusion URL filter
  • Better handling of large (e.g. 3+MB JSON payloads)

Exclusion filters in the search field:

  • data will match "data"
  • -data will match anything that doesn't contain "data"
  • "-data" will match "-data"
  • -"-data" will match anything that doesn't contain "-data"

0.18.0

Network Inspector is now a helper app written with Kotlin Multiplatform. It's still packaged inside Snap-O.app, but as an inner helper app.

Now that KMP has been introduced, it'd be nice if everything ended up with KMP. With a nice AVPlayerView in a Swing panel, maybe it's possible..

0.17.0

Some payload format updates.

Network events are now wrapped in a "FeatureEvent" payload wrapper, to support other features sending messages via the "Snap-O Link Server" in the future.

0.16.0

Liquid glass support

0.15.0

  • Max response payload size: 5MB
  • Image preview support
  • Change sort order of network requests
  • "Waiting for ADB server..." alert will not trigger while Snap-O is in the background.

0.14.1

Maintains window order when re-opening Snap-O.

0.14.0

Logcat Viewer by @angus-oai

Tools now available from the capture window toolbar.

0.13.0

Network Inspector will re-open on launch.

0.12.0

Collapsible JSON pretty printing view
More performant handling of large response bodies

0.11.0

Early work on network inspector (alpha)

0.10.0

  1. "Bug Report" option for screen recording (--bugreport)
  2. "Show Touches on Capture" works again
  3. Preview strip improvements: Drag 'n drop from the thumbnails, and device name hints
  4. Ensure each simultaneous capture gets a unique filename

0.9.0

Removed most of the animated transitions throughout the app, to make it feel even snappier.

0.8.0

Simultaneous device captures

Don't capture the wrong device by accident, anymore. Capture all of them!

  1. When you take a screenshot or screen recording, Snap-O does it across all your connected devices simultaneously.
  2. Next/Previous Device now moves between the captures you had just taken.
  3. Screen recordings only show up if they have a non-zero duration.

0.7.0

Snap-O floats over other windows during a screen recording, to make it easier to use alongside an emulator in Android Studio.

0.6.0

  1. Faster time to first screenshot
  2. ADB path no longer needs to be set
  3. Live Preview has some basic touch support
  4. Other UX/perf improvements

0.5.0

Initial Snap-O release!

item.title: Snap‑O 13.0.1
item.description: - Fixed dragging full and cropped recordings from capture review into apps such as Slack, with accurate video previews and export progress.

item.title: Snap‑O 13.0.0
item.description: - Review and crop screenshots or recordings before saving them to Capture History or dragging a copy into another app. - Use ⇧⌘V to both start and stop recording. - Android tool builds recover automatically from damaged managed Node installations.

item.title: Snap‑O 12.0.0
item.description: - Type, copy, and paste directly in Live Preview. - Screen recording now has a live preview so you can continue interacting with the device in Snap-O while you record. - Rotate physical devices and emulators with the same controls and keyboard shortcuts. - Use new capture shortcuts: ⇧⌘S for screenshots, ⇧⌘V for recording, and ⌘Y for Capture History. - Delete selected captures with Delete or ⌘Delete.

item.title: Snap‑O 11.2.0
item.description: - Select multiple captures in Capture History and delete them together. - Start Live Preview faster. - Recognize running emulators sooner and keep device names consistent across windows. - Fix a crash when an emulator connection fails or is cancelled. - Place Volume Up above Volume Down in the left control bar.

item.title: Snap‑O 11.0.0
item.description:
- New: Device Manager -- Manage existing Android emulators and connected devices. Start, stop, or cold boot emulators, then open them directly in Live Preview. - Command-drag instead of Option-drag from Live Preview to export a screenshot while ordinary dragging controls the device.
Device Manager uses your existing Android SDK and AVDs. SDK installation, AVD creation and editing, and a custom SDK location picker are not included in this version.
